correctness.rationale: In the two-move Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game, a first selected point is classified by colour and the four existential possibilities of a different red/blue member inside/outside its E-class. Matching these characters in both structures is both necessary and sufficient to answer the second move. Capping each class colour count at two and each of eight nonzero class-shape multiplicities at two preserves every possible two-move response. All 3^8−1=6560 profiles are then exhaustive (not an extrapolation). Independently recomputed both the direct quantifier-free one-point type partition and the five-bit formula: exactly 207 groups with minimum-size distribution 2,6,10,17,22,28,30,29,26,18,12,5,2 (sizes 1..13); both extremal profiles require size 13.
residual_risks: Reliance on exact 6560-profile enumeration after analytic two-move reduction; unrestricted additional predicates/ranks are not included.
